scenarios.title: Someone Is Still Inside
scenarios.description: You escaped a burning house, but your younger brother says his pet is still inside.

choices.text: Go back in quickly to get the pet
choices.feedback: Never go back into a burning building. Smoke and heat can overcome you in seconds.

choices.text: Stay outside and call the fire service
choices.feedback: Correct. Once you are out, stay out. Firefighters have the equipment and training to search safely.

choices.text: Ask a neighbour to run in and fetch it
choices.feedback: Sending anyone back in puts another life at risk.

scenarios.title: Heater by the Curtains
scenarios.description: You notice a space heater running right next to the living room curtains.

choices.text: Leave it, since it has an automatic shut-off
choices.feedback: Heaters are a leading cause of home fires. Flammable items need to be kept well away from them.

choices.text: Switch it off and move it 3 feet away
choices.feedback: Correct. Keep anything that can burn at least 3 feet from heat sources, and turn heaters off when you leave the room.

choices.text: Tie the curtains back so they do not touch it
choices.feedback: Tied curtains can still catch fire from the heat. Move the heater away instead.

scenarios.title: Fire in the Oven
scenarios.description: Food in your oven catches fire and flames are visible through the glass door.

choices.text: Open the door and blow out the flames
choices.feedback: Opening the door feeds the fire with oxygen and can send flames into your face.

choices.text: Pour a bucket of water into the oven
choices.feedback: Water can spread burning grease and is dangerous around electrical appliances.

choices.text: Turn the heat off, keep the door shut
choices.feedback: Correct. Keeping the door closed starves the fire of oxygen. If it does not go out, leave and call emergency services.

scenarios.title: Alarm in the Tower
scenarios.description: The fire alarm rings in a multi-storey building where you are on the 8th floor.

choices.text: Take the elevator since it is quicker
choices.feedback: Elevators can stop working or open onto the fire floor. Do not use them during a fire alarm.

choices.text: Wait at your desk until it is confirmed
choices.feedback: Treat every alarm as real. Delays cost you valuable escape time.

choices.text: Leave at once and take the stairs
choices.feedback: Correct. Use the stairs, stay calm, and go to the assembly point outside.

scenarios.title: Flood Watch Tonight
scenarios.description: A flood watch is announced for your area. It is not raining hard yet.

choices.text: Prepare: check your route and pack essentials
choices.feedback: Correct. A watch means flooding is possible, so use the time to prepare.

choices.text: Ignore it because the rain is still light
choices.feedback: Conditions can change fast. A watch is your chance to prepare before a warning.

choices.text: Do nothing until water starts entering the house
choices.feedback: By the time water enters your home, escape routes may already be cut off.

scenarios.title: Evacuation Order
scenarios.description: Authorities order your neighbourhood to evacuate because of rising floodwater. Your family wants to stay and protect the house.

choices.text: Stay and move your belongings upstairs first
choices.feedback: Possessions can be replaced, people cannot. Roads can flood quickly and cut off escape.

choices.text: Take a flooded shortcut to save time
choices.feedback: Flooded roads may hide washed-out sections. Turn around, don't drown.

choices.text: Leave now by the official evacuation route
choices.feedback: Correct. Follow evacuation orders early and stick to the official routes.

scenarios.title: Going Home After the Flood
scenarios.description: The rain has stopped and the water outside is going down. You want to go home and check the damage.

choices.text: Go home now and walk through the water
choices.feedback: Floodwater can be contaminated, electrified, and hide debris and holes.

choices.text: Wait until officials say it is safe
choices.feedback: Correct. Roads and buildings may still be unsafe even after the water drops.

choices.text: Send a child ahead to see if it is safe
choices.feedback: Children are at even greater risk from floodwater and hidden hazards.

scenarios.title: Water in the Basement
scenarios.description: Floodwater has entered your basement, where the electrical panel and outlets are.

choices.text: Wade in and unplug all of the appliances
choices.feedback: Standing water and electricity can be deadly. Never enter a flooded area with live power.

choices.text: Stay out and call the electric utility
choices.feedback: Correct. Stay out and let professionals make the power safe.

choices.text: Run an electric pump to drain it
choices.feedback: Using electrical equipment around standing water risks electric shock.

scenarios.title: Tornado Watch
scenarios.description: A tornado watch is issued for your area this afternoon.

choices.text: Stay alert and know where your shelter is
choices.feedback: Correct. A watch means conditions are right for tornadoes. Prepare to move quickly.

choices.text: Go outside to look for the tornado first
choices.feedback: Tornadoes can be hidden by rain or darkness. Do not wait to see one.

choices.text: Carry on as normal and ignore alerts
choices.feedback: Alerts change quickly. Staying informed gives you time to act.

scenarios.title: Warning Signs in the Sky
scenarios.description: The sky turns dark green, large hail begins to fall, and you hear a loud roar like a freight train.

choices.text: Take shelter in the safest place nearby
choices.feedback: Correct. These are classic tornado warning signs. Act right away, do not wait for a siren.

choices.text: Stop to film it for social media
choices.feedback: Every second outside increases your risk from flying debris.

choices.text: Open the windows to equalize pressure
choices.feedback: Opening windows does not protect your home and wastes time you need for shelter.

scenarios.title: Blackout in the Storm
scenarios.description: A storm knocks out the power at night and your home is completely dark.

choices.text: Light several candles around the house
choices.feedback: Candles are a common cause of home fires. Use flashlights or battery lamps.

choices.text: Use flashlights or battery lamps
choices.feedback: Correct. Flashlights are the safest source of light during a power outage.

choices.text: Run a gas stove for light and warmth
choices.feedback: Using a stove this way risks fire and harmful gas build-up.

scenarios.title: Fallen Power Line
scenarios.description: After the storm, you find a power line lying on the ground in your yard.

choices.text: Move it aside with a wooden broom handle
choices.feedback: Never touch or move a downed line, even with an object. Treat it as live.

choices.text: Stay back and report it to the utility
choices.feedback: Correct. Assume every downed line is live. Stay well back and report it.

choices.text: Step over it carefully and keep going
choices.feedback: Electricity can travel through the ground around a downed line.

scenarios.title: Aftershock
scenarios.description: The main shaking has stopped. While you are checking your home, the floor starts shaking again.

choices.text: Assume it is over and keep walking
choices.feedback: Aftershocks can be strong enough to cause more damage. React the same way every time.

choices.text: Drop, cover, and hold on again
choices.feedback: Correct. Treat every aftershock like the main quake.

choices.text: Run outside past the damaged walls
choices.feedback: Weakened walls and falling debris make moving during shaking dangerous.

scenarios.title: Shaking in the Mall
scenarios.description: An earthquake hits while you are in a crowded shopping mall.

choices.text: Run for the nearest exit with the panicking crowd
choices.feedback: Crowds and falling objects make running dangerous. Protect yourself first.

choices.text: Drop, cover, and hold on under a sturdy table
choices.feedback: Correct. Protect your head and neck, and wait until the shaking stops before moving.

choices.text: Stand in the open middle of the hallway
choices.feedback: Open areas offer no protection from falling signs, lights, and glass.

scenarios.title: Strong Shaking at the Beach
scenarios.description: You are at the beach when severe earthquake shaking lasts for more than 20 seconds.

choices.text: Wait on the sand to see what the water does
choices.feedback: A tsunami may arrive within minutes. Do not wait for a visible sign.

choices.text: Move to high ground or inland right away
choices.feedback: Correct. If severe shaking lasts 20 seconds or more, a tsunami may follow. Move inland or to high ground right away, without waiting for a warning.

choices.text: Swim out past the breaking waves
choices.feedback: Do not enter the water. Currents and waves can be deadly.

scenarios.title: Smell of Gas
scenarios.description: After the shaking stops, you smell gas inside your home.

choices.text: Flip the light switch to see better
choices.feedback: A spark from a switch can ignite a gas leak.

choices.text: Light a match to locate the leak
choices.feedback: A flame near leaking gas can cause an explosion.

choices.text: Open a window and get out quickly
choices.feedback: Correct. Get out, avoid any spark, and call for help from a safe distance.

scenarios.title: Not Responding
scenarios.description: A man collapses in front of you. He does not respond when you shout and is not breathing normally.

choices.text: Call for help and start chest compressions
choices.feedback: Correct. Call for help, then push hard and fast in the centre of the chest until help arrives.

choices.text: Give him water and wait for him to wake up
choices.feedback: Do not give anything by mouth to an unresponsive person. He needs urgent help.

choices.text: Leave him to rest and check on him later
choices.feedback: Every minute without circulation reduces survival chances.

scenarios.title: Burn With a Blister
scenarios.description: Your friend's hand was burned and a blister has formed.

choices.text: Press ice on the burn to cool it
choices.feedback: Ice can damage the skin further. Cool burns with clean, cool running water instead.

choices.text: Cover it loosely and get medical care
choices.feedback: Correct. A burn that blisters needs medical care. Cover it loosely with a clean, dry, non-adhesive dressing.

choices.text: Stick an adhesive bandage over it
choices.feedback: Adhesive bandages stick to the skin and can cause further damage.

scenarios.title: Coughing but Choking
scenarios.description: A coworker is choking on food but is coughing loudly and can still speak.

choices.text: Let them keep coughing and stay close
choices.feedback: Correct. A strong cough is the best way to clear the airway. Step in only if they can no longer cough, speak, or breathe.

choices.text: Slap them hard on the back right away
choices.feedback: Interfering with an effective cough can move the object deeper.

choices.text: Give them a big glass of water to drink
choices.feedback: Drinking while the airway is partly blocked can make choking worse.

scenarios.title: Accident on the Road
scenarios.description: You see a motorcycle crash on a busy road. The rider is lying on the lane and cars are still passing.

choices.text: Rush straight to the rider at once
choices.feedback: You could become a second victim. Check for danger before you approach.

choices.text: Check it is safe, then call for help
choices.feedback: Correct. Making sure the scene is safe protects you and the injured person.

choices.text: Drive off since others will help
choices.feedback: Everyone assuming someone else will help is how people end up without help.
